required_outcomes: Moves the oven on: asks the landlord to approve an appliance repair engineer (or sends the approved job to provider selection) now that the settings have not helped.

Hands the deposit protection question to a human on the lettings or compliance team with a packet (deposit £1,150, moved in June, no certificate or scheme information received), treating it as time-sensitive because protection and prescribed information have a 30-day legal deadline.
Routes the rent date change to the person who can agree it (landlord or lettings team) instead of agreeing or refusing it.
Replies to the tenant: the oven is being moved on, and the deposit and rent-date questions have been passed to the right team who will come back to her.
acceptable_alternatives: Putting the deposit and rent-date questions in one handover, provided both are named and the deposit point is marked as the time-sensitive one.
Asking the tenant when and how the deposit was paid, in the same reply, to complete the handover.
positive_behaviours: Keeps the oven on its own track so the tenancy questions do not delay the repair.
Uses a non-emergency priority (P2 or P3) for the tenancy handover.
red_flags: Telling the tenant her deposit is protected, or that it is not, without checking.
Answering only the oven and ignoring the deposit and rent-date questions.
prohibited_actions: Agreeing to change the rent date without the landlord's agreement.
Telling the tenant she must pay a fee above £50 for changing the rent date.
critical_failures: The deposit protection question is lost: not passed to anyone and not answered.
